texts: Remodelling techniques should be considered obsolete for pediatric patients with connective tissue disorders: A.
Remodelling replaces the sinuses but leaves the annulus unsupported, so in these patients it tends to dilate and the valve leaks again.
Reimplantation (the David operation) fixes the annulus inside the graft and has become the preferred valve-sparing operation in children and young adults with these disorders.
Replacing the root does not end the disease, since the rest of the aorta stays at risk, and Ehlers-Danlos patients carry a much higher surgical risk because of fragile tissues.
In the picture, the free collar stretches and leaks, while David's reimplanted mouth stays tight.
Memory hook: in a child, leave no collar free.
